Theme

adverb noun

also adverbs, adverb of place, adverb of time, adverbs of place, adverbs of time, interrogative adverb

classical

Quint. 1.5.50: intrō et intus locī adverbia (Lewis & Short cites the passage)
Prisc. p. 1003 P.: pars ōrātiōnis indēclīnābilis, cujus significātiō verbīs adjicitur (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 220, 231, 245

adverbium, adverbiī n.

noun, second declension

an adverb

The word “added to the verb”, ad verbum. Its kinds go in the genitive: adverbium locī, of place (Quintilian’s phrase), temporis, of time, numerī, of number (Traupman 231). Adverbs do not decline: sunt indēclīnābilia (Traupman 232).

Examples

  • hoc amplius intrō et intus locī adverbia, eō tamen intus et intrō sum soloecismī sunt

    moreover intrō and intus are adverbs of place, yet eō intus and intrō sum are mistakesQuint. 1.5.50

  • Dā adverbia locī.

    Give some adverbs of place.Traupman 231

  • Adverbium quid est?

    What is an adverb?Traupman 231

See also part of speech, verb, modify, indeclinable.
